project.objective: Who were the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico, and what were his exact birth date and place?

questions.question: Who were the parents of Mauro Cruz Corona, born about 1910 in or near Nueva Italia, Michoacán, Mexico?
questions.rationale: Mauro's parentage is entirely unestablished in the tree. Mexican civil birth registers (and parallel Catholic baptismal registers) for c. 1910 Michoacán record the child's exact date and place of birth alongside both parents' names and origins, making the birth-record search the single most efficient path to answering all parts of the objective simultaneously. Sibling stubs (Miguel, Liborio, Facundo Cruz) with 1913–1918 births in Guerrero localities (La Unión and Coahuayutla) suggest the family may have migrated between Guerrero and Michoacán, providing additional search context in registers of both states.

items.rationale: The Michoacán statewide civil birth register (collection 1916243) is name-searchable and 100% indexed for 1910 per the locality guide (loc_001). Per Mexico_Naming_Customs wiki, Mauro's compound surname Cruz Corona identifies his father's first surname as Cruz and his mother's first surname as Corona — search on Cruz (paternal) with Corona (maternal). A civil birth acta names both parents directly. The locality guide confirms the documented civil-register gap covers only 1913-1915 and 1918, so 1910 records are fully available.

The Parácuaro Catholic baptismal register (collection 1883388) is name-searchable and 96% indexed with full-text search, covering 1906-1921 per the locality guide (loc_001). Baptisms were recorded in parallel with civil registration and name the child's parents and godparents. This is the primary parallel source alongside item pli_001, and it covers the 1913-1915 civil gap years. Search Cruz (paternal) and Corona (maternal) per Mexico naming customs.

The locality guide (loc_001) identifies a second chapel — Santa Ana, El Caulote (formerly Furicato) — serving part of Parácuaro municipality, with bautismos 1902-1918 indexed on FamilySearch. If Mauro's family resided in the El Caulote area rather than the main parish center, his baptism would appear here rather than in collection 1883388 (item pli_002). Search here if item pli_002 yields nothing.
items.skip_reason: pli_002 (Parácuaro Catholic baptisms) produced positive results — Mauro's 1941 marriage record and a sibling record both name parents Sostenes Cruz and Ma Apolinar Corona — so this El Caulote chapel fallback was never triggered.

items.rationale: Three siblings recorded in the tree were born in Guerrero during the exact years Parácuaro's civil register has documented gaps: Miguel Cruz (24 Apr 1913, El Coco, La Unión, Guerrero), Liborio Cruz (23 Jul 1916, Pochutla, Coahuayutla, Guerrero), and Facundo Cruz (27 Nov 1918, Rosario, Coahuayutla, Guerrero). The Guerrero civil registration collection (collection 1918291) is name-searchable. Each sibling's birth acta would name the same father (surname Cruz) and mother (surname Corona) as Mauro's record, directly establishing both parents' full names. Search Cruz and Corona in La Unión and Coahuayutla municipalities for each sibling's name.

If the siblings' civil birth records in collection 1918291 (item pli_004) are absent for La Unión and Coahuayutla, the Guerrero Catholic church records (collection 1823323) are name-searchable and may hold the siblings' baptismal entries for the same period. Catholic baptisms name both parents. The collection covers 1576-1979 and includes parishes in both La Unión and Coahuayutla municipalities.

BCG standards require a dedicated search for the candidate parents' marriage. The father's surname is Cruz and the mother's is Corona (established by Mauro's compound surname per Mexico naming customs). They married before Mauro's birth circa 1910, most likely 1895-1910; the date window is bounded by the plausible marriage age of the parents. A civil marriage acta names both parties' parents (Mauro's grandparents), confirms the couple as a unit, and supplies the mother's full given name and her own maternal surname. Michoacán civil marriage volumes for Parácuaro are available on FamilySearch via the statewide civil registration collection (collection 1916243).

Mauro Cruz Corona died 21 April 1999 in Nueva Italia (Parácuaro municipality), Michoacán per the tree. Mexican civil death actas (defunciones) routinely name the deceased's parents by full name. This record carries secondary information (from whoever reported the death), but independently may confirm or supply parent names when birth and sibling records are absent or inconclusive. The date range is sized to the death year, not the birth window; files can testify to birth-era events. Search via the Michoacán statewide civil registration collection.

Per the Mexico_Military_Records wiki, Cartillas del Servicio Militar Nacional were issued to all males entering military service at age 18 and list the conscript's full name, date and place of birth, parents, and civil status. Mauro born ~1910 would have registered ~1928 at the Parácuaro ayuntamiento. These records are NOT on FamilySearch; they are held in the local ayuntamiento or at the Dirección General de Archivo e Historia, Miguel de Cervantes Zaavedra s/n, Col. Irrigación, 11640 México D.F. (SEDENA). Searching this record requires a written request to SEDENA or the Parácuaro ayuntamiento and is best attempted after FamilySearch sources above are exhausted.
items.skip_reason: SEDENA cartillas are not online; retrieval requires written correspondence to the Dirección General de Archivo e Historia (SEDENA, México D.F.) or the Parácuaro ayuntamiento. Not executable in autonomous research.

quirks: Nueva Italia (also called Colonia Nueva Italia) is not a separate FamilySearch place — all civil and parish records are filed under Parácuaro municipality. Search Parácuaro for all records.

Civil nacimientos have documented gaps: years 1913, 1914, 1915, and 1918 produce no indexed volumes in FamilySearch volume_search, and the FamilySearch Catalog film note for this municipality explicitly lists only Nacimientos 1910-1912, 1916-1917, 1919-1922 on film DGS 4871475. Those four years appear absent from the civil record; use Catholic bautismos as the parallel and substitute source.

Catholic bautismos for 1906–1921 are available and 96–97% name-indexed on FamilySearch (collection 1883388). These volumes cover the entire target period, including the gap years missing from civil registration.

The catalog creator for the Parácuaro parish registers is Archivo Diocesano de Apatzingán, but a separate catalog note also references archivo diocesano de Zamora. Both archives may hold copies; in 1905–1920 the Tierra Caliente was under the Diocese of Zamora before the Diocese of Apatzingán was created in 1961.

A second chapel — Santa Ana, El Caulote (formerly Furicato), with bautismos 1902–1918 indexed on FamilySearch — also serves part of Parácuaro municipality. If a family cannot be found in the main Parácuaro parish, search El Caulote as well.

No FamilySearch named collections were returned by collections_search for Michoacán in the 1905–1920 window, but the civil and parish volumes are fully available through volume_search (100 total volumes, all online) and the statewide FamilySearch collections 1916243 (civil) and 1883388 (Catholic church).

Civil registration in Mexico was established at the municipio level by law on 28 July 1859 and was vigorously enforced from 1867 onward, per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration. For births before that enforcement, only Catholic parish records exist.

The sibling evidence (Miguel, Liborio, Facundo Cruz born 1913–1918 in Guerrero localities) suggests the family may have been in neighboring Guerrero during the years missing from Parácuaro's civil register. Guerrero civil registration is also online at FamilySearch (collection 1918291, 1860-1996). Search both states.

Parácuaro is in the Tierra Caliente region. Adjoining municipalities include Apatzingán (northwest), Tepalcatepec (southwest), and La Huacana (east). If no record appears for Parácuaro, check neighboring municipios at FamilySearch.
All records are in Spanish. The Spanish Genealogical Word List at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Spanish_Genealogical_Word_List is the primary paleography aid for these records.

# Locality Guide: Nueva Italia (Parácuaro Municipality), Michoacán, Mexico (1905–1920)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Parácuaro municipality recognized 1861. Nueva Italia (Colonia Nueva Italia) is a community within this municipality and has no separate civil or ecclesiastical record-keeping jurisdiction.
- **Administrative center:** Parácuaro (the municipio seat), Michoacán
- **Parent jurisdiction:** State of Michoacán (became a Mexican state 22 December 1823); civil records held at the municipio level
- **Population during period:** No population data was returned by FamilySearch tools for this municipio. Nueva Italia is in the Tierra Caliente (hot lowlands) region of Michoacán.
- **Economy:** Agriculture, including large hacienda and colonization enterprises (Nueva Italia was itself a colonization project in the Tierra Caliente).
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic, overwhelmingly dominant. The Parácuaro parish church is Nuestra Señora de la Asunción; a subsidiary chapel at El Caulote (Santa Ana) also served the municipio.
- **Key historical events:** The Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) disrupted civil registration compliance throughout Michoacán, directly explaining the documented gaps in Parácuaro's civil nacimientos for 1913–1915 and 1918.

## Boundary changes
- Parácuaro municipality has been stable since its 1861 formation. No boundary changes affecting the target period were returned by the place tools.
- The Diocese of Apatzingán, which currently holds the parish archive, was created in 1961 from the Diocese of Zamora. In 1905–1920, Parácuaro was under the Diocese of Zamora. The physical records are now at Archivo Diocesano de Apatzingán (per FamilySearch Catalog, koha:162793), but the catalog notes also reference Archivo Diocesano de Zamora — both archives may hold copies.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Municipio-level civil registration began 28 July 1859 (national law); vigorously enforced from 1867 (per [Mexico Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration)). Parácuaro filmed nacimientos start at 1881.
- **What exists — nacimientos (births):** Continuous volumes, 100% name-indexed, online for 1900–1912 and 1916–1922 (within the target period). A documented gap: no civil nacimientos volumes for 1913, 1914, 1915, or 1918 appear in either FamilySearch volume_search or the Catalog. The Catalog film note for DGS 4871475 explicitly lists only "Nacimientos 1910-1912, 1916-1917, 1919-1922."
- **Key target volumes (all 100% indexed, online via collection 1916243):**
  - 1910: DGS 004871475_001_M98X-BWN (53 images) — most relevant for Mauro born ~1910
  - 1911: DGS 004871475_002_M98X-BWJ (61 images)
  - 1912: DGS 004871475_003_M98X-BWV (70 images)
  - 1916: DGS 004871475_004_M98X-BWK (72 images)
  - 1917: DGS 004871475_005_M98X-BPZ (47 images)
- **What a nacimiento record contains:** Date and time of birth; child's name and gender; parents' names, ages, birthplaces, residence, marital status; paternal and maternal grandparents' names.
- **Where held:** Originals at Archivo del Registro Civil del Estado de Michoacán. Online at FamilySearch collection [Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859-1940](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1916243) and Ancestry [Michoacan, Mexico, Civil Registration Births, 1859-1934](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60415/).

### Church records
- **Parish:** Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Parácuaro — the main parish. Subsidiary chapel Santa Ana, El Caulote (formerly Furicato), recorded its own bautismos.
- **Archive:** Archivo Diocesano de Apatzingán (catalog creator); catalog notes also reference Archivo Diocesano de Zamora.
- **Bautismos coverage for target period (all online, FamilySearch collection 1883388):**
  - 1890–1906: DGS 004087255_002 — 98% indexed, full-text searchable
  - 1906–1913: DGS 004737524_001_M9ZR-WQ1 — 96% indexed, full-text searchable
  - 1913–1917: DGS 004737524_002_M9ZR-W7M — 97% indexed, full-text searchable
  - 1918–1921: DGS 004737525 — 97% indexed, full-text searchable
- **El Caulote / Santa Ana chapel:** Bautismos 1902–1918 (DGS 4768334, indexed) and 1918–1936 (DGS 4768335, indexed), via collection 1883388.
- **What a bautismo record contains:** Date and place of baptism; child's name, gender, and birth date; legitimacy; parents' names; godparents' names.
- **Language:** Spanish. Records in this period are handwritten in formatted ledger registers.
- **Key point:** The Catholic bautismos fill the 1913–1915 and 1918 gaps in civil registration. Both record types should be searched even when both exist, as they contain different information.

### Census records
- **1930 National Census:** The only digitized national census available; covers Parácuaro municipio. FamilySearch: [Mexico Census, 1930](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1307314) (DGS 4107250, indexed, online). Also at Ancestry.
- **Earlier enumerations:** No earlier census found for this municipio in the tools.

### Probate and court records
- No probate records for Parácuaro were returned by the FamilySearch Catalog — a cataloguing gap, not necessarily evidence of absence. Originals likely at the municipio courthouse or state archive in Morelia.

### Land records
- Nueva Italia was a large colonization enterprise; land concession records may be at the AGN in Mexico City (http://www.agn.gob.mx/). No Parácuaro land records identified as digitized.

### Military records
- Mexican Revolution service records held at SEDENA (https://www.gob.mx/sedena). Limited online access; written request required.

### Cemetery records
- [FindAGrave index for Michoacán](https://www.findagrave.com/cemetery/search?cemetery-name=&cemetery-loc=Michoac%C3%A1n+de+Ocampo%2C+Mexico) and BillionGraves. Sexton records for Parácuaro not confirmed as digitized.

### Newspaper records
- No local newspaper identified for Parácuaro in 1905–1920. [Hemeroteca Nacional Digital de México](http://www.hndm.unam.mx/) has some historical state papers.

### Immigration/emigration records
- Border crossings Mexico to US: Ancestry collection https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1082 (1895–1964); FamilySearch collection 1803932 (1903–1957).
- Internal migration between Guerrero and Michoacán is not recorded in border records; search civil registers of both states.

### Tax records
- Property and personal property tax records held at municipal and state archives. Not identified as digitized for Parácuaro.

### Other record types
- **Confirmaciones:** Parácuaro, 1900–1923 (DGS M9ZR-4M5, 0% name-indexed, full-text searchable — must be browsed). Useful for identifying siblings.
- **Información matrimonial (pre-marriage investigations):** 1898–1925, all 100% name-indexed online. Name both sets of parents and witnesses — excellent for identifying parents of anyone who married in Parácuaro.

---

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859–1940 (collection 1916243) | Free |
| FamilySearch | Mexico, Michoacán, Catholic Church Records, 1555–1996 (collection 1883388) | Free |
| FamilySearch | Mexico Census, 1930 (collection 1307314) | Free |
| Ancestry | Michoacan, Mexico, Civil Registration Births, 1859–1934 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60415/) | Subscription |
| Ancestry | Michoacán, Mexico, Catholic Church Records, 1649–1909 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60021) | Subscription |
| Ancestry | Mexico, Select Baptisms, 1560–1950 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/9297/) | Subscription |
| MyHeritage | Mexico Baptisms, 1560–1950 (https://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-30039/mexico-baptisms-1560-1950) | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** 100 digitized volumes match Parácuaro, Michoacán in the 1900–1925 window (summary complete: true). All are online; no physical-only volumes among those surveyed.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Archivo del Registro Civil del Estado de Michoacán, Morelia | Original civil registers for Parácuaro | In-person or written request |
| Archivo Diocesano de Apatzingán | Original parish registers, Parácuaro and El Caulote | In-person or written request |
| Archivo Diocesano de Zamora | May hold additional copies of parish registers (per catalog note) | In-person or written request |
| AGN, Mexico City (http://www.agn.gob.mx/) | Land concessions, military, colonial records | In-person; some online |

---

## Records NOT online
- Civil nacimientos for 1913, 1914, 1915, and 1918 — no volumes exist at FamilySearch; Catholic bautismos (which ARE online) are the only available substitute.
- Probate and court records for Parácuaro.
- Land and tax records for Parácuaro.
- SEDENA military service records.
- Sexton / cemetery records.

---

## Known record losses
No tool result in this survey explicitly states that any Parácuaro record set was destroyed. The gap in civil nacimientos for 1913–1915 and 1918 is consistent with Revolutionary-era disruption of registration compliance, but the catalog and volume_search do not state those records were destroyed — they may exist in physical form at the state civil registry. The Catholic bautismos appear intact through this entire period.

---

## Research tips
1. **Search civil nacimiento 1910 (DGS M98X-BWN) and parish bautismo 1906–1913 (DGS M9ZR-WQ1) simultaneously** at FamilySearch — both are indexed and free. Per [Mexico Research Tips and Strategies](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Research_Tips_and_Strategies): always search siblings' birth records to confirm and extend parentage findings.
2. **Search información matrimonial records (1898–1925, 100% indexed)** for a marriage of Mauro's parents before 1910. These pre-marriage investigation documents name the groom, bride, both sets of parents, and witnesses — a direct path to grandparental names.
3. **Search El Caulote (Santa Ana chapel) bautismos** (DGS 4768334, 1902–1918, indexed) if the main Parácuaro parish search yields nothing. Parish served different parts of the municipio.
4. **Search Guerrero civil records (FamilySearch collection 1918291)** in parallel. The sibling stubs place the family in Guerrero during 1913–1918 — exactly the years absent from Parácuaro civil nacimientos.
5. **Search the 1930 census.** Mauro Cruz Corona (~age 20 in 1930) should appear in the Parácuaro enumeration; household entry may name parents' birthplaces and ages.
6. **Account for name variants and transcription errors.** Per [Mexico, Michoacán, Catholic Church Records how-to](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico,_Michoac%C3%A1n,_Catholic_Church_Records_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records): abbreviations and alternate spellings are common. Browse nearby images after any index search.
